draft.title: Introduced species
card: An introduced species is a species brought into an ecosystem where it did not live before. People bring them in on purpose or by accident.
Native species are the ones that belong in an ecosystem. An introduced species can change their numbers, because the native species have not lived alongside it before.
the introduced species uses the same food, water or shelter as a native species. European rabbits eat plants that native animals also need.
the introduced species preys on native species or is poisonous to them. Cane toads carry poison, and native predators that eat them can die.
draft.remember: An introduced species can change native populations by competing with, eating or poisoning them.

opts: A species brought into a place it did not live before
A species that has lived in a place for a very long time
A species that has become rare in a place
A species that feeds only on the plants of a place
a.why: An introduced species is one that has been brought into a new ecosystem by people, on purpose or by accident. A native species belongs there, so a species that has lived there for a long time is not introduced.
a.clue: Think about where the species lived before.

b.q: Cane toads are poisonous. In a billabong in the Northern Territory, many native goannas die after eating cane toads. How have the toads changed the goanna population?
opts: By poisoning them, which lowers their numbers
By competing with them for food, which lowers their numbers
By eating them, which lowers their numbers
By sharing the habitat, which raises their numbers
b.why: The goannas die because the toads carry poison, so the toads change the population by poisoning. Competing is a tempting answer, but it means using the same food or shelter, and the goannas here are dying from eating the toads, not from a shortage of resources.
b.clue: Look at what happens to the goannas after they eat the toads.

a.best: A species brought into a place it did not live before

b.best: By poisoning them, which lowers their numbers
